reasons.reader_question: The letter question is sharp, and the fire adds a second concrete one. The fire's link to the Ladder is blurred by muddled geography.
reasons.change: Ila moves from oath-bound to a first chosen, announced omission. She also gains the 'carried' clue and sight of the lakes and an enemy fire.
reasons.romance_movement: There is a new exchange: her costly omission against his first free name. Her refusal of the promise has a fresh, rule-based reason.
reasons.shown_chemistry: The pacing song on the hard pitch, the 'Possibly four. I was eleven' banter, the thumb on the rope and the handed-back sentence all show attraction through action.
reasons.character_logic: Ila is sound. Kunal's swing from 'Then take it back. Draw it' to 'Promise me you never will' has no visible trigger.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: The cost is named and personal: the spring audit, the Chief Surveyor title and eleven winters. The promise refusal carries the risk of a lost hand.
reasons.prose: The prose is clean and concrete, with few AI tells and one em dash. The sheet monologue spends the word 'dodge' before the dialogue can land it.
reasons.continuity: Rope length, the promise rule, the oath sworn at nineteen, the omission history, Mini's age and Raghu's day lead on the north-east fork all match the facts.

fixes: At 'and it came out at the foot of that shoulder' (Twists without setup): this contradicts 'far head of the basin' and 'a night's walk off', and leaves the threat unclear. Rewrite it so the fire is placed to watch the whole basin floor below the Ladder. Every step they take from the niche will be in its view, and the one way down Taravan can't name is now the way Raghu's men are watching.

At 'Then take it back.' He was turning the loose end (Irrational behaviour): Kunal releases her, then within a page demands a lifelong promise with no trigger. Add the cause. Ila's line 'I'll have to find the sentence that's true' should land on him as proof she will file the Ladder at the audit one day. Have him say so briefly before he lays the rope down.

At 'A sheet that was true and incomplete. She knew' (Endless monologue, echo): Ila calls her own omission a dodge before Kunal does, which flattens his 'And it's a dodge.' Cut the 'dodge' sentence and the phrase-knowing line. Also replace 'I don't know yet if that's a lie, but it isn't one that costs anything. I've checked' with a plain statement that a blank on paper isn't a lie to him.
reader_question: What will Ila do when she reaches the Glass Lakes with the queen's letter, and whose fire is watching the basin?
new_facts_assessment: The fire on the shoulder is necessary as the ending hook and fits F485 and F690 (Raghu's two pairs a day ahead, heading to the overlook). It is already logged as F695. The prose wrongly places the Ladder's exit 'at the foot of that shoulder', although the fire is at the far head of the basin, a night's walk away.
